title: Design relational scalability and data protection
learningObjective: Recommend how a relational database scales (up, read scale-out, pools, sharding, Hyperscale) and how its data is protected (encryption, masking, row-level security, auditing, threat protection).
foundation: When a database gets busier you can give it more power (scale up), send reads to copies (scale out reads), share resources across databases (pools), or split the data across databases (sharding).
Protecting data means encrypting it, hiding what people shouldn't see, limiting which rows they read, and recording who did what.
engineer: Scalability: vertical scaling changes vCores or service objective online (brief reconnect); read scale-out routes ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly connections to a readable replica (Business Critical, Premium, Hyperscale); Hyperscale adds high-availability replicas and up to 30 named replicas for read workloads; elastic pools for many databases; horizontal sharding with elastic database tools (shard map manager) for data beyond one database; geo-replicas can also serve reads in other regions.

Encryption: TDE encrypts data at rest by default (service-managed or customer-managed key in Key Vault); TLS for data in transit; Always Encrypted encrypts sensitive columns in the client driver so the database engine and DBAs never see plaintext (secure enclaves allow richer queries).

Access to data: Microsoft Entra authentication for users and managed identities; dynamic data masking hides values in results for non-privileged users (not encryption); row-level security filters rows with security predicates; ledger tables give tamper evidence.

Monitoring and threat protection: auditing to storage, Log Analytics or Event Hubs; Microsoft Defender for SQL (vulnerability assessment, threat detection such as SQL injection alerts); data discovery and classification. Network protection: private endpoints and disabling public access.

animation.caption: Pick a scaling technique and the right data protection feature.

example.title: Scaling and securing a payments database
body: The Business Critical database routes reporting to its readable replica with ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly and scales up for month-end. Card numbers use Always Encrypted; support staff see masked phone numbers.
Row-level security limits each merchant to its own rows. Auditing goes to Log Analytics, and Defender for SQL alerts on injection attempts.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription; most design reviews need only Reader access
permissions: Reader to review existing resources; Contributor or Owner to build the design
limits: Check service limits and regional availability for each component
portal: SQL database > Compute + storage: scale vCores; Read scale-out setting.
SQL database > Security: Auditing, Dynamic data masking, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Transparent data encryption.
configuration.cli:
az sql db update -g rg-data -s sql-contoso -n db-pay --capacity 16
az sql db audit-policy update -g rg-data -s sql-contoso -n db-pay --state Enabled --lat-destination-type LogAnalytics --log-analytics-workspace-resource-id <law-id>

lab.objective: Choose how to scale and protect each database.
steps: Answer every case in both trainers.
expected: Read scale-out for reports; sharding for data beyond one database
Always Encrypted hides data from DBAs
failureScenarios: Using masking as if it were encryption
Scaling up when reads could go to a replica
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: Reports still hit the primary after enabling read scale-out.
troubleshooting.fix: Add ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly to the reporting connection string.

troubleshooting.symptom: A DBA can still see credit card numbers.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Always Encrypted for those columns.

comparisons.difference: TDE protects files at rest; Always Encrypted protects columns from anyone without the client key, including DBAs.

comparisons.service: Dynamic data masking vs row-level security
comparisons.difference: Masking hides parts of values; RLS hides whole rows.

misconceptions.reality: It only changes what non-privileged users see in results.

misconceptions.myth: Scaling up is the only way to handle more load.
misconceptions.reality: Read scale-out, pools and sharding also help.

architectureDecisions: Route reads to replicas before scaling up.
Always Encrypted for highly sensitive columns.
Auditing + Defender for SQL on production.

steps.label: Problem
steps.title: Busier every month, and full of sensitive data
body: The database slows at month-end, reports compete with orders, and auditors ask who can see card numbers.

steps.label: Scale
steps.title: Four ways to scale
body: Scale up: more vCores. Read scale-out: send reports to a readable replica. Elastic pool: share resources across databases. Sharding: split data across databases by a key.

steps.label: Encrypt
steps.title: At rest and in use
body: TDE encrypts database files (on by default). Always Encrypted encrypts chosen columns in the app's driver, so even DBAs see only ciphertext.

steps.label: Control
steps.title: Hide, filter, record
body: Dynamic data masking shows XXXX-1234 to support staff. Row-level security returns only a user's own rows. Auditing and Defender for SQL record and alert on suspicious activity.

callout.text: Masking is not encryption — privileged users still see the real values.
